summary:
Xenoterra is a website designed to help researchers identify terrestrial analogues on Earth that share physical and environmental characteristics with the Moon and Mars. Our project focuses on supporting rover mobility research by making it easier to find locations on Earth that can serve as potential testing environments.
The website brings together information about relevant environmental and surface conditions, allowing users to explore and compare Earth locations with conditions found on the Moon and Mars. This helps researchers to identify potentially suitable places to investigate rover performance in challenging terrain and environments.
Mobility is essential for future lunar and Martian exploration, particularly for transporting equipment, accessing resources and supporting development of permanent bases. However, rovers must be able to operate reliably in unfamiliar and demanding conditions. By making terrestrial analogue locations easier to identify, Xenoterra aims to support more informed rover testing and contribute to the development of reliable mobility systems for future space exploration.

Use of Super Intelligence

Super Intelligence tools were used to assist with aspects of project development, including prototyping, refactoring and selective code generation. All output code were reviewed, tested and adapted by the team before intergration. The project architecture, implementation decisions, testing and validation were carried out and reviewed by the team.
